Display signs and posts blown over on top of automobiles at Ramirez Ford.

Roma police department relayed report of quarter size hail in vicinity of Falcon Dam and Falcon Heights in Starr County.
A trained spotter reported wind gusts of 59 mph in a thunderstorm which moved through El Sauz early in the evening.
Law enforcement in Starr County reported numerous trees blown down on FM 649 near El Sauz.

Power lines down, and power outages, were reported across a large part of Starr County as a developing line of severe thunderstorms moved through. One of the strongest cells likely produced some of these power outages between Viboras and La Gloria along Farm-to-Market road 2686.
Law enforcement in Starr County reported power lines down and power outages occurred in Roma due to high winds from strong to severe thunderstorms in and near the area.
Quarter size hail was reported near El Sauz.
Penny sized hail was reported near the intersection of Farm to Market Roads 755 and 490.

The Roma Police Department in Starr County reported hail up to one inch in size fell in the city of Roma during a thunderstorm which moved through the area.

Hidalgo S.O. relayed report from the general republic of 1.5 inch hail west of San Isidro.
Public reported 50 to 60 mph winds between Falcon and Lopeno.
Quarter size hail reported between Falcon and Lopeno.
Quarter sized hail fell across northeast portions of Starr County. United States Postal Office and a coop observer reported hail between 4:20 pm and 4:40 pm between San Ysidro and La Gloria.
Wind gust up to 60 mph was reported by a Co-op observer near San Isidro.
Public reported multiple large tree limbs down FM 755.
Trained spotter reported quarter size hail and provided a video that suggested hail up to half dollar size fell.
Trained spotter reported wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph in Rio Grande City.
Starr County Sheriffs Office reported quarter size hail at the intersection of FM 1367 and Eisenhower Road.
Starr County Sheriffs Office reported shingles blown off of a roof and damage to the walls of a structure in Alto Bonito.
Public reported via social media golf ball size hail in El Sauz.
COOP observer at Falcon Dam reported the front and back windows of a front end loader shattered.
Public posted video on social media showing hen egg size hail falling on a carport on La Sagunada Road north of Rio Grande City.
Media reported portion of roof blown off of house in Fronton. Several trees were blown down as well. Time estimated via radar imagery.
Public reported half dollar size hail in Fronton.
Starr County Sheriff's Office reported utility pole blown down by thunderstorm winds on Lucianos Road in Escobares. Time estimated by radar.

Facebook reports relayed to the NWS office in Brownsville reported two large hail reports east of Rio Grande City: Golfball sized hail 4.6 miles east, near La Puerta, and half-dollar sized hail (1.25) 4 miles east southeast of Rio Grande City near Los Velas road.

A newspaper report from Starr County indicated a large restaurant sign blew onto a vehicle and caused an unknown amount of damage to the vehicle during the passage of a thunderstorm in Rio Grande City a little after 8 PM on April 25th.
Multiple trees were reported down and blocking roadways to the north of La Gloria near highway 755. Time estimated via radar.
Social media public reported ping pong sized hail in Starr County.
Hail with a diameter of 2 inches was reported by the Roma City Police Department.
Rio Grande City Police Department reported that dime-size hail fell for about 2 to 3 minutes around 415 PM CDT.

An NWS Storm Survey team on the way out to the City of Zapata noted at least a dozen mainly mesquite, live oak, and ebony trees large limbs blown down between Rio Grande City and Roma. A social media report also noted an uprooted tree in the Escobares area. Time was estimated via…
Thunderstorm winds estimated at 50 knots peeled the roof off of a mobile home and blew debris several feet along La Sagunada Road in Starr County west of FM755.

A homeowner interviewed by a local television station reported ping pong to golf ball sized hail, which damaged his roof and several of his windows. He also reported severe damage to trees, shingles, and a destroyed wooden playground due to very gusty winds.

Social media posts showed a destroyed metal baseball backstop along with several large tree limbs down on the northern side of Rio Grande City. Timing estimated by radar and social media posts.
A social media post showed damage to several metal sheds and a metal carport roof on the north side of US Hwy 83, behind Norma's, in Garciasville. Timing estimated from radar and social media posts.
A storm chaser reported hail up to one inch in diameter at 3:34PM CDT until 3:45PM CDT April 21st approximately 7 miles west of La Gloria, TX.
Storm chaser reported hail up to 1 inch in diameter just west of La Gloria.
Employee at the Falcon Heights Motel and RV Park reported hail the size of quarters.

Report via social media of damage to trees, billboards, and utility poles in the city of Roma that occurred between 11:10PM CDT and 11:35PM CDT. Damage confirmed by phone call to Roma Police Department.
Roma Police Department reported hail the size of golf balls in the city of Roma.
Member of the public shared a picture of hail estimated to be about the size of a quarter.
McDonalds in Roma at 104 East Grant Street reported hail the size of quarters.
Member of the public shared pictures of half dollar to ping pong ball hail along Suntex Road in Starr County. Hail sizes are estimated based off pictures. Time estimated by radar.
Video on social media shows a tree down near the intersection of Suntex Road and HWY 83 in Starr County. Timing based on radar.

Member of the public shared a picture of a large tree limb, the base of which was approximated 6 to 8 inches in diameter, from a Mesquite tree blown across FM2360 near La Victoria in Starr County. Time is estimated based on radar.
Public reported estimated ping pong size hail on FM 3167 in Rio Grande City with a picture on social media. Time estimated from radar.
Half dollar size hail was reported along FM 755 north of town. Report received via the internet.
Quarter size hail was reported just north of Rio Grande City, via web report.
Nickel to quarter size hail was reported. This was estimated by a resident and by video with a small cell behind earlier cells near Rio Grande City.
There was a social media report of 1.5 inch diameter hail in Fronton, Texas (Starr County).
There was an mPING report of golf ball size hail about 5.6 miles west-northwest of Rincon, or about 16.5 miles northeast of Rio Grande City.
Pictures and video showed ping pong to golf ball size hail about 8.7 miles north-northeast of Rio Grande City.
A ranch owner sent a video of estimated quarter size hail.
